title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the entity's activities, including any Director; determined by the Company to be its Directors and employees reporting directly to the Managing Director. Also referred to as 'restricted person' in the exceptions clause.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: Distinguished only for approval routing: the Chairman's own dealings require prior Board approval rather than Chairman approval, and the Chairman approves other KMP's dealings.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates of a KMP, such as family members, family trusts and family companies. The insider trading prohibition extends to dealings through them, and post-trade notification covers dealings by or through Associates.

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's Annual Report
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's Annual Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Half Year Report
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Half Year Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's quarterly reports (if applicable)
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's quarterly reports

rules.detail: Trading in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities (i.e. derivatives) is banned outside open Trading Windows; within a window it is subject to the same prior written approval of the Chairman/Board as any other dealing.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from trading outside Trading Windows in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Hedging is not named as a distinct concept. A hedge (e.g. a purchased put) is a financial product created over the Company's securities, so it is caught by the section 4.3 derivatives rule: confined to open Trading Windows and requiring prior written Chairman/Board approval.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from trading outside Trading Windows in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named. A prepaid forward or similar would be a financial product created over or in respect of the Company's securities and so is caught by the same Trading Window and prior approval regime as other derivatives.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from trading outside Trading Windows in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named. The Policy applies to 'the sale and purchase of any securities', so a short sale would be treated as an ordinary sale requiring the same prior written Chairman/Board approval and Trading Window compliance; the Policy does not separately address how the shares would be borrowed.
rules.evidence: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue from time to time.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not named but are a financial product created over or in respect of the Company's securities, so they are confined to open Trading Windows and require prior written Chairman/Board approval.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from trading outside Trading Windows in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending arrangements giving lenders rights over the KMP's interest in the Company's securities are prohibited unless Board approval is obtained; the Board must not withhold approval unreasonably.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into Margin Lending arrangements whereby lenders are provided with rights over their interests in the company's securities unless Board approval is obtained, such approval not to be withheld unreasonably.

rules.detail: Granting a lender rights (e.g. a mortgage or charge) over the KMP's interest in Company securities requires Board approval, not to be unreasonably withheld; a resulting sale on default is separately excused from the insider trading rules (see exceptions).
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: Any arrangement giving a lender rights over a KMP's interest in Company securities (not limited to formal margin loans) requires Board approval, not to be unreasonably withheld.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into Margin Lending arrangements whereby lenders are provided with rights over their interests in the company's securities unless Board approval is obtained, such approval not to be withheld unreasonably.

rules.detail: Short-term trading is banned outright with no defined holding period, except selling shares shortly after exercising options.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within five (5) business days of the transaction
clearance.evidence: Any Key Management Personnel (other than the Chairman) wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman or the Board before doing so.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within five (5) business days of the transaction
clearance.evidence: If the Chairman wishes to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities, the Chairman must obtain the prior approval of the Board before doing so.

carve_outs: exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter
short_term.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

exceptions.evidence: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or all other Board members if the applicant is the Managing Director)
exceptions.evidence: Key Management Personnel who are not in possession of inside information ... may be given prior written clearance by the Managing Director ... to sell or otherwise dispose of Company securities in a Closed Period where the person is in severe financial hardship

Exceptional circumstances includes: court order, a court enforceable undertaking such as a bona fide family settlement, to transfer or sell securities of the Company, a significant circumstance determined by the non-interested Board, or a legal or regulatory requirement to do so.
trade under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under an employee incentive scheme (as that term is defined in the ASX Listing Rules)

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

make an investment in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel: trigger = before entering any arrangement giving a lender rights over their interest in Company securities; to whom = the Board; deadline = prior to entering the arrangement, with Board approval not to be withheld unreasonably.

exemption_authority: Managing Director (or, for the Managing Director, all other Board members) may grant written exemption from a Closed Period for severe financial hardship or exceptional circumstances (court order, court-enforceable family settlement, Board-determined significant circumstance, or legal/regulatory requirement), specifying the time period for the sale; confidentiality of the grant or refusal is not addressed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement ... a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is an express, automatic exception, available at any time including in a Closed Period, without needing separate clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into Margin Lending arrangements whereby lenders are provided with rights over their interests in the company's securities unless Board approval is obtained, such approval not to be withheld unreasonably.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of the collar, secured over the collared shares, needs upfront Board approval, but the Board cannot unreasonably refuse it, giving a workable (if not guaranteed) path.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collared shares (or the call exercise/put exercise settlement) exceed these thresholds, the unwind must be pre-discussed with the Board and legal advisers and documented before execution, adding a process step beyond ordinary approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the shares to be collared are being funded via a cashless option exercise, that funding sale must occur outside Closed Periods, which can constrain timing of when the collared parcel becomes available.

summary: A funded collar is achievable in substance but requires two layers of Board-level consent. The put and call legs are 'financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities' under section 4.3, so they may only be traded within an open Trading Window and require the prior written approval of the Chairman (or the Board, for the Chairman) under section 5.1, with post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within five business days. The loan secured on the collared shares falls within the section 4.3 restriction on arrangements giving a lender rights over the KMP's interest in Company securities, so it needs prior Board approval, though that approval must not be withheld unreasonably. Critically, a subsequent forced sale by the secured lender on default, including during a Closed Period, is expressly carved out as a permitted exception and confirmed not to breach the insider trading rules, giving the bank comfort on enforcement. Unwind or settlement volumes above 10% of the executive's holding or 10% of 20-day average traded volume must additionally be discussed with the Board and legal advisers before execution.
